tasks.short: Plan a study of operational problems, evidence needs and improvement options.

steps.what: Agree the problem, scope and intended decisions with the study sponsor
Collect operating records and existing procedures for the agreed scope
Reconcile records and calculate baseline volumes, delays and costs
Choose hypotheses, study methods, sampling and measures
Write the study plan, evidence requests, milestones and resource needs

loop.input: Study approach, study brief, baseline pack and approved study template.
loop.output: Study plan with source references and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections, dates and totals. Analyst checks source support and methodological consistency.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per plan. Unresolved claims remain flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but the rationale must connect situational evidence to the selected methods.

steps.what: Approve the study scope, resources and access conditions

tasks.design: A reusable study workspace on the {WORKFLOW} collects the brief and retrieves permitted evidence from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}. Deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce a baseline pack for the {BI}; a bounded drafting loop assembles the analyst's chosen approach into a study plan in the {DOCS}. The sponsor approves scope and resources before the study starts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence crossed systems with inconsistent definitions. Templates could structure a plan but could not choose a sound study method.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, metric checks and document generators. Bounded drafting can turn an explicit study approach into readable prose.
tasks.still_hard: Causal inference, representative sampling and agreement on the real problem remain difficult. Missing timestamps and disputed cost allocations can invalidate the baseline.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst frames a testable problem and challenges a sponsor's preferred explanation.

ambition.what: A rapid diagnostic study for small operational teams without dedicated analysis support.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing competing explanations and less time collecting records. A delegated mandate could let them choose diagnostic methods within an approved study budget; budget approval stays with the sponsor.

reach.task: Turn the approved study into a dependency and resource plan.
reach.learn: Critical paths, resource constraints and change control.

reach.task: Design a study of order delays using operational event data.
reach.learn: Queueing, event timestamps and service-level measures.

evidence.claim: Permissioned extracts, deterministic baseline calculations and templated study plans are established technical patterns.
A documented Deloitte report case contained nonexistent citations, supporting source checks on generated study text.
AI used to evaluate workers can fall within the EU AI Act's Annex III employment category.

assumptions: This is a scoped operational study, not an automated individual employment decision.
Record collection includes access requests and export retrieval, so its share exceeds pure screen-reading time.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to personal data. EU AI Act applicability depends on actual use; consultation follows national rules.
Consent and access estimates cover an ordinary review; formal consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Which operating records are accessible and under what permissions?
Are metric definitions and process identifiers consistent across systems?
Will the study assess individual workers or only operational processes?
Which national consultation rules and internal approval routes apply?
research_questions: Do recorded timestamps measure actual waiting time or only administrative entry time?
Does a structured study template provide enough value without model drafting?
Which proposed causes survive comparison with alternative explanations?
new_work: Resolve data exceptions and maintain metric definitions.
Check draft claims against the evidence pack.
Maintain connectors, templates and access rules.
Review whether new study uses change privacy or consultation requirements.

tasks.short: Interview staff and observe work to understand actual processes and resource use.

steps.what: Prepare interview questions and an observation checklist

loop.input: Approved study plan, existing procedures and a question library.
loop.output: Interview guide and observation checklist linked to study questions.
loop.check: Analyst checks coverage, neutral wording and whether questions fit the work setting.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass. Analyst writes unresolved or sensitive questions manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed question library cannot fully adapt to undocumented procedures and situational study questions.

steps.what: Arrange interviews and observation visits around staff availability
Interview staff about work, exceptions, handoffs and practical constraints
Observe work on site and record methods, equipment, delays and workarounds
Consolidate notes into process findings and unresolved questions

loop.input: Analyst-written interview notes and observation logs, with study questions.
loop.output: Findings draft separating observed facts, reported claims and analyst interpretations.
loop.check: Require source references for findings. Analyst checks omissions, contradictions and inappropriate attribution.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per evidence batch. Ambiguous notes remain open questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe similar activities differently and require contextual grouping.

steps.what: Confirm factual descriptions and record disputed interpretations

tasks.design: A study workspace in the {WORKFLOW} prepares guides from approved material in the {DOCS} and coordinates visits through the {CALENDAR}. Interviews and observation remain human; a bounded loop converts analyst-written notes into traceable findings for participant validation. Access controls in the {DOCS} restrict identifiable notes separately from wider study findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observation depends on physical context and trust. Notes varied in structure, making synthesis slow and difficult to trace.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable forms and scheduling configuration reduce coordination. Bounded extraction can organise notes while preserving links to the analyst's evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Staff may describe the official process rather than actual practice. Observation can change behaviour, and disagreement cannot be settled by summarising notes.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst notices workarounds, asks tactful follow-up questions and earns candid explanations.

ambition.what: Include rotating-shift staff in process discovery through shorter, prepared visits.

tasks.altitude: Most of the week still involves interviews and observation. Less preparation and note assembly creates room for follow-up visits; formal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Observe a process and distinguish procedural gaps from justified local adaptations.
reach.learn: Evidence sampling, nonconformity definitions and corrective-action interviews.

reach.task: Investigate how workplace layout contributes to delays.
reach.learn: Site access, physical constraints and safe observation practices.

evidence.claim: Scheduling configuration and structured observation forms can reduce administration without replacing fieldwork.
Bounded extraction can organise free-text notes, but factual interpretation still needs human checking.
The EU AI Act prohibits workplace emotion recognition, subject to its stated exceptions.

assumptions: The workflow uses analyst-written notes; it does not require audio, video or automated emotion inference.
The time split keeps most effort in direct conversation and observation, consistent with the supplied priors.
Participant validation confirms factual descriptions; it does not give participants a veto over independent conclusions.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR governs identifiable notes. Access, retention and employee consultation follow applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which shifts, locations and roles need representation?
Can participants speak confidentially without their line manager present?
What note retention, attribution and employee consultation requirements apply?
Who can authorise safe access to operational sites?
research_questions: Do shorter prepared visits capture the same exceptions as longer unstructured interviews?
Does extraction preserve minority accounts and contradictions?
Does participant validation reveal systematic gaps in observation?
new_work: Check extracted findings against original notes.
Resolve contradictions through further interviews or observation.
Maintain question libraries and observation checklists.
Apply note access, retention and deletion rules.

tasks.short: Write operating manuals and train staff to use changed procedures, forms and equipment.

steps.what: Gather approved changes, current policies and equipment instructions
Draft the manual with steps, forms, examples and exception routes

loop.input: Approved procedure sources, equipment instructions and a manual template.
loop.output: Manual draft with source-linked instructions and flagged source conflicts.
loop.check: Validate document structure and references. Analyst walks through steps and checks exceptions against sources.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section. Conflicting or unsupported instructions go to the process owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot translate varied source documents into clear, role-specific instructions.

steps.what: Approve procedural accuracy, responsibilities and policy alignment
Publish the approved manual and replace the superseded version
Prepare role-specific exercises, quick guides and understanding checks

loop.input: Approved manual, role profiles and training templates.
loop.output: Role-specific exercises, quick guides and proposed answer keys.
loop.check: Analyst tests exercises against the manual. Training lead approves accuracy and audience suitability before use.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per role. Unclear answers or unsafe exercises require manual revision.
loop.why_not_simpler: Layout is deterministic, but useful scenarios and explanations depend on the changed procedure and audience.

steps.what: Invite affected staff and arrange training sessions
Demonstrate the procedure, coach practice and address staff questions
Record attendance, completion and follow-up training needs

tasks.design: A controlled generator assembles approved material from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, then uses bounded loops to draft manuals and training packs. Existing approval and versioning in the {DOCS} release the manual, while the {WORKFLOW} coordinates invitations through the {CALENDAR} and records trainer-confirmed outcomes in the {LMS}. Live coaching remains human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source documents and training materials drifted apart. Producing consistent role-specific instructions required repeated writing and formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Document APIs, version controls and reusable generators reduce assembly work. Bounded drafting can adapt approved instructions into exercises without inventing a new procedure.
tasks.still_hard: A readable manual can still describe an impractical procedure. Equipment training may require physical demonstration and competence checks by a qualified person.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees where learners struggle, adjusts explanations and distinguishes a training gap from a flawed procedure.

ambition.what: A role-specific change clinic using staff questions and practical exercises after each major procedure release.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time formatting manuals and more time coaching difficult transitions. With delegation, they can choose training formats and targeted follow-up; process owners retain procedure approval.

reach.task: Plan adoption support for a changed office procedure.
reach.learn: Service standards, staff coverage and adoption measures.

reach.task: Maintain controlled procedures and verify training effectiveness.
reach.learn: Document control, competence evidence and corrective-action follow-up.

evidence.claim: Document versioning, publication approvals, enrolment and completion records can use existing software configuration.
Source-grounded drafting can assist manual preparation, but procedural accuracy requires walkthroughs and accountable approval.
A documented Deloitte report case illustrates that generated text can contain nonexistent sources.

assumptions: The typical baseline includes a document store and basic learning records; their exact capabilities need confirmation.
Training records use trainer-confirmed attendance and explicit completion rules, not inferred worker competence.
The split preserves substantial writing and live training time, consistent with the supplied priors.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to learner records. National rules may require consultation when training records become worker monitoring.
unknowns: Which document approval, versioning and learning features are already licensed?
Which procedures require safety, legal or specialist approval?
Do any qualifications require observed practical assessment?
Are translations, accessible formats or offline training materials required?
Which consultation requirements apply to learning records and assessment?
research_questions: Can a learner complete the procedure using only the generated manual?
Do role-specific exercises improve practical performance over a generic presentation?
Can source changes reliably identify which training materials need revision?
new_work: Walk through generated instructions and verify answer keys.
Handle failed enrolments and incomplete training evidence.
Review recurring learner questions and revise the procedure or training.

tasks.short: Review forms and reports with managers and users, then agree improvements to purpose, format and distribution.

steps.what: Collect current forms, report samples and distribution lists
Inspect source fields, report runs and available usage records
Compare fields, frequency and recipients to flag duplication and gaps
Discuss purpose, usability, missing information and distribution with managers and users
Draft recommendations and revised form or report specifications

loop.input: User requirements, review findings, comparison results and relevant policy.
loop.output: Change proposal and specification with each change linked to a requirement or finding.
loop.check: Validate required fields and change traceability. Analyst checks meaning, access implications and unresolved conflicts.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per proposal. Conflicting requirements stay flagged for decision.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text requirements need contextual synthesis; fixed templates cannot explain trade-offs or reconcile terminology.

steps.what: Approve which forms and reports to change, retain or retire
Copy approved actions into a separate tracking workbook

tasks.design: An inventory service links forms in the {DOCS} to report metadata from the {ERP} and {BI}, then applies deterministic checks for repeated fields, stale schedules and recipient differences. A bounded loop drafts specifications from confirmed user requirements, while the process owner records change or retirement decisions in the {WORKFLOW}. Those approved records become delivery items in the {PROJECT}, removing the separate {SPREADSHEET} tracker.
tasks.previous_blocker: No single inventory connected document versions, report definitions and recipients. Usage evidence rarely explained why a form or report mattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata connectors and deterministic comparisons make the inventory maintainable. Bounded drafting reduces the effort of turning discussions into traceable specifications.
tasks.still_hard: Low usage does not prove low value. Rarely used reports may support controls, legal duties or emergency decisions, and users may disagree on essential fields.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst establishes what decision each report supports and negotiates between user needs, controls and administrative burden.

ambition.what: A quarterly decision on retiring redundant management reports.

tasks.altitude: The analyst shifts from collecting examples to facilitating decisions about information needs. With an agreed mandate, they can prioritise the review queue; report retirement still requires owner approval.

reach.task: Translate approved report changes into field, validation and access requirements.
reach.learn: Data lineage, schema constraints and acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Identify superseded forms while preserving required records.
reach.learn: Retention schedules, version control and record classification.

evidence.claim: Metadata inventories and deterministic comparisons can identify candidate duplication without deciding business necessity.
A single approved action record can feed delivery tracking and remove duplicate workbook maintenance.
Usage records involving identifiable employees require a GDPR assessment; national consultation requirements depend on the use.

assumptions: Some report metadata and usage records are available; missing usage remains unknown rather than zero.
Initial comparisons use explicit field mappings and exact rules; semantic matching is not assumed.
Validated findings are reused when a broader organisational study exists.
Approval records can become the authoritative change tracker.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
Usage analysis concerns report utility, not individual worker evaluation.
unknowns: Which report definitions, distribution lists and usage records can be retrieved?
Who owns each form, report and retention decision?
Which apparently redundant reports serve legal, audit or contingency needs?
Can the approval record replace the separate tracking workbook?
Does usage collection introduce employee monitoring under national rules?
research_questions: How often do deterministic duplication flags identify a genuinely removable report?
Does low report usage predict low decision value?
Can users complete representative work with the revised form or specification?
new_work: Maintain field mappings and comparison rules.
Verify generated specifications against user requirements.
Investigate low-usage reports before proposing retirement.
Check that approved changes reach delivery and obsolete versions are withdrawn.

role.altitude: The management analyst spends more time framing studies, observing work and negotiating practical changes. Preparation, evidence assembly and document production become lighter; any new authority to prioritise studies or training must be explicitly delegated.
reach: Project management specialists: turn approved findings into sequenced delivery plans.
Computer systems analysts: translate process needs into testable system requirements.
Quality control systems managers: connect procedure changes to controlled documents and competence evidence.
Logistics analysts: investigate operational delays using event data and field observation.
skills_to_grow: Study design, sampling and causal reasoning.
Change facilitation, privacy assessment and national consultation procedures.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a repeatable operational diagnostic service for teams without dedicated analysts: establish a baseline, observe real work, test competing explanations and take a measurable improvement proposal to the responsible manager.
